body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Saturday, October 17, and the story leading the day is a frightening one that turned into something quietly moving — the East Bakersfield–Foothill football game was stopped before halftime after a medical emergency on the East High sideline. Otherwise, the valley is calm: expect a high near 91 under clear skies, air quality sitting at a moderate 65, no weather alerts in effect, and crews still working one active fire in the county, the Cyrus Fire. Grab your coffee — here's what happened while you slept.

## The Kern Overnight

The biggest call of the night came shortly after 1:15 a.m., when a commercial building near 30th Street and Union Avenue caught fire. Crews arrived to find the loading dock involved and power lines down along one corner of the structure. They set up a command post at the intersection and closed the northbound side of the road while they worked. Firefighters knocked the flames down from the outside first, then moved in to finish off the interior fire, and reported the primary search clear. No injuries were reported.

Fire carried the rest of the night too. Multiple callers reported smoke showing from an apartment window in the 3400 block of Wible Road in southwest Bakersfield, where Truck 7, Truck 1 and two battalion companies were assigned to a second-floor unit in a two-story complex and knocked the fire down. A grass fire was also reported near Cottonwood and Bradshaw.

Elsewhere, police ran a foot chase that ended near Lincoln and Robinson streets in east Bakersfield, with Air 1 overhead talking units onto one person detained on the 1200 block of Lincoln Street — officers were told the man came out of the passenger seat of a car that had been stopped and had tried to get into a house before he was caught. A domestic call in the 7000 block of Willis Avenue turned up a report of a gun, and officers also worked an assault in which a caller said she was held down and had her phone taken. Two crashes drew responses: one at 18th and H streets that left vehicles blocking the roadway, and a single-car wreck on Mohawk Street that sent two people to the hospital by ambulance. A semi was reported driving the wrong way with bright headlights on Highway 58. The log also shows a commercial fire alarm at a hotel on East Brundage Lane that crews traced without finding a fire, a pursuit in Arvin, and a report of a blue sedan stolen from a parking area.

## Today's weather

It's 57 degrees right now at Meadows Field, on the way to a high near 91 this afternoon — a warm, clear October Saturday. Tonight's low settles around 63. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and air quality is moderate at 65, which is fine for most folks but worth noting if you're sensitive and planning to spend the afternoon outside. Fire crews remain on one active fire in the county, the Cyrus Fire. If you're headed to the chalk festival or a ballgame, it's a sunscreen-and-water kind of day.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that Friday night's East Bakersfield–Foothill football game was stopped before halftime because of a medical emergency on the East High sideline.** According to 23ABC, the Trojans had just taken a 17–0 lead with under two minutes left in the half when play came to an abrupt halt. An ambulance drove onto the track near the 40-yard line, followed by Kern County Fire Department vehicles. A Foothill player and someone on the East sideline told 23ABC that a member of the visiting team's staff collapsed in what they believed was a heart attack, though authorities have not confirmed that or released any information about the person's condition. After the person was taken away, players, cheerleaders and coaches from both schools gathered at midfield for a prayer. The game did not resume and was declared final, with Foothill taking the win — a result that matters a great deal, since the Trojans had forfeited all seven of their previous victories over eligibility violations involving two players and now need to win both of their remaining games to reach the playoffs.

**KGET 17 also has the rest of Week 9 high school football scores from around Bakersfield and Kern County**, so if you're tracking a team's playoff path, that roundup is the place to find Friday's results.

**The California Highway Patrol says a pedestrian suffered major injuries in a collision in Oildale, according to KGET 17.** Details on the circumstances were limited in the initial report, but the CHP is handling the investigation. It's a reminder of how quickly things change for people walking along some of our busier corridors, especially after dark.

**23ABC is reporting exclusively that a Bakersfield man was detained by ICE while on his way to work, and his business partner is raising concerns about how he was treated.** David Rivera, owner of D-R Building Solutions, told the station he got a call from his business partner, Sergio, as the detention was unfolding — Sergio said he'd been pulled over by unmarked vehicles and believed it was ICE. Rivera said he could hear what was happening over the phone and grew worried, particularly when Sergio mentioned a lawyer and, in Rivera's words, it didn't seem to matter. Sergio was able to give Rivera his location before the call ended; Rivera later arrived to find the truck on the side of the freeway with a broken window. Video from the Rapid Response Network of Kern shows the truck on the shoulder. Rivera said Sergio's family is distraught. Authorities have not released information about Sergio's status or the reason for the stop.

**And a note from Bakersfield Now: Six Flags Over Georgia has reopened following a deadly fall from its Goliath coaster, though that ride remains closed.** It's a national story with local reach, since plenty of Kern families make that trip.

## Something good

The Via Arté chalk festival has turned a parking lot at the Marketplace on Ming Avenue into a walk-through gallery, with more than 100 artists at work. It's free and runs today and tomorrow from 9 a.m. to 8 p.m., with reservations available at viaartebakersfield.com — you can also buy a 2-by-2-foot square and make your own. Bakersfield Museum of Art marketing manager Lauren Marty told 23ABC the tradition reaches back to Italian street painters who made art on the pavement, something an everyday working person could actually see. Proceeds support the museum's exhibitions, art education and community programs. This year 22 high school teams are competing alongside featured artist Anitta Meza, who started in the student competition 13 years ago and is now creating a 12-by-15-foot piece inspired by words from her aunt, who is battling stage-four thyroid cancer — and it glows in the dark.

## Coming up this week

It's a busy stretch at City Hall. The Historic Preservation Commission meets Tuesday, October 20, at 10 a.m., and the Special Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meets the same day at 2 p.m., followed by the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission at 2 p.m. On Wednesday, October 21, the City Council holds a 3:30 p.m. session and then its regular meeting at 5:15 p.m. — two separate agendas, so check which one has your item before you head down.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full slate. The AiAi & Tekla Comedy Tour lands tonight, October 17. Fortune Feimster brings her "Taking Care of Biscuits" tour Sunday, October 18. Monday, October 19, is the Cults & Classics screening of "Psycho." Switchfoot plays with special guest Anberlin on the Forever Now Tour Wednesday, October 21, and Henry Cho's Empty Nest Tour comes through Friday, October 23. If you're already thinking ahead to next season, the Cults & Classics Season Pass for 2026–2027 is on sale now.

Have a good Saturday, Bakersfield — stay cool out there, and if you're near Ming Avenue, go see what a hundred chalk artists can do to a parking lot.

top.title: East Bakersfield-Foothill football game stopped due to medical emergency on sideline
